clue.text: "New Look" sort: rich and, from the outset, innovative and iconic

definitions.text: "New Look" sort: rich and, from the outset, innovative and iconic

indicators.note: something new is freshly made, so the letters that follow are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its opening letter, taken here from both innovative and iconic

parts.note: only its opening letter is used
the same from-the-outset instruction applies: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A fashion type hailed as wealthy, innovative and iconic, the way a magazine might praise a style legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted "New Look" seems a single title, but New also tells you to rearrange the letters, and the whole clue then describes the designer who launched that 1947 collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The French couturier launched the 1947 collection the press christened the New Look, and was rich, innovative and iconic.

clue.text: Forestall the usual demand of Wonderland royal?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to intercept and prevent

definitions.text: the usual demand of Wonderland royal?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Queen of Hearts' constant cry, "Off with his head!"

explanation.walkthrough: The Queen of Hearts in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland keeps ordering beheadings.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off trouble is to block it before it arrives, preventing it in advance.

clue.text: "Fancy!" = "Indeed"

parts.note: the equals sign is read as the word is
ay is an old or dialect yes, indeed

explanation.walkthrough: The equals sign is read aloud as "is".
explanation.definitionFit: I say! is an exclamation of mild surprise, just as Fancy! is.

clue.text: Number one song

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the top one, the finest
second meaning: a hit song, best known in Tina Turner's 1989 version

explanation.walkthrough: Number one suggests a chart-topping song, but it is a separate meaning: the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the finest of all and is also the title of a famous 1980s pop anthem.

clue.text: British PM's remains left inside

indicators.note: the word for left goes inside the word for remains

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
to quit is to leave; quit as past tense means left

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's ashes left inside an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith was the Liberal Prime Minister of Britain from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Ruin house party?

parts.note: a do is a party
in means at home, in the house

explanation.surface: A house party that trashes the place.
explanation.walkthrough: A house party is a do held in, so the phrase splits into its two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To do in is slang for to destroy or kill, i.e. wreck completely.

clue.text: I introduced the family

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
seeds introduced into soil are sown

explanation.surface: Someone saying they introduced the family to another person.
explanation.definitionFit: One's own are one's relatives, kin, as in caring for one's own.

clue.text: Would it feel unusual having students round?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters have the students inside them
an unusual arrangement of these words' letters is needed

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
L is the learner-driver plate, so two students are LL

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a room would feel strange with students around.
explanation.walkthrough: Round is the definition, in the sense of plump, not the preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-filled-out describes a plump, curvy body, rounded rather than thin.

clue.text: Style of working girl might put on injury cover

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece is put on top of the second

parts.note: might is power or strength
a dressing covers a wound

explanation.surface: Fashion advice on the look a career woman might adopt, with a bandage thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: "Working girl" sounds risqué but means a career woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Power dressing is the 1980s fashion of sharp suits worn by professional women to convey authority.

clue.text: Morning eructation's beginning following cheese and beans

indicators.note: the morning and belch pieces come after the cheese in the answer

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

indicators.note: the beginning of the word eructation is its first letter

parts.note: eructation is a belch; only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A burp in the morning after eating cheese and beans, a mildly embarrassing breakfast scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young green soya beans served in the pod, popular as a Japanese snack.

clue.text: Even now zero energy cuts agreed

indicators.note: the energy letter cuts into the word for even, splitting it

parts.note: now that debts are settled we are quits, i.e. even

explanation.surface: An announcement that, even at this late stage, cuts to zero energy use have been agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite so is a formal phrase of assent, said when you agree with what someone has just said.

clue.text: Aerobatic manoeuvre in which we go quiet

parts.note: a loo is where we go, in the euphemistic sense of going to the toilet

explanation.surface: A stunt pilot's manoeuvre during which everyone falls silent in awe.
explanation.walkthrough: "We go" is the coy toilet sense; loo is the British word for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a stunt in which an aircraft flies a full vertical circle.

clue.text: Giant hit US railway's rolling stock, express part of it

definitions.note: a stock of words, the part of a language used to express things

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the hit and the railway together are read backwards

parts.note: in cricket a six is the biggest hit, clearing the boundary
the El is the elevated railway of US cities such as Chicago

explanation.surface: A big crash hits an American railway's rolling stock, with an express train involved.
explanation.walkthrough: "Rolling stock" looks like a single railway term, but rolling is the reversal signal and stock begins the definition. A six is cricket's biggest hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lexis is a language's vocabulary, its whole stock of words available for expression.

clue.text: Any of Earth's five divisions: the last first, the first last

indicators.note: the alphabet's last letter goes first in the answer
the first number goes last in the answer

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
one is the first number

explanation.surface: A geography-test instruction about the five climatic belts, phrased like a biblical saying about first and last.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrasing echoes "the last shall be first, and the first last"; here it is literal instructions about letters and numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographers divide the globe into five climatic belts: torrid, two temperate and two frigid.

clue.text: Staff at walkabout not working properly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shepherd's or bishop's hooked stick
second meaning: Australian slang for broken or ill

explanation.walkthrough: A walkabout is an Aboriginal Australian's journey, so "at walkabout" points to Australian usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a hooked staff, and in Australian English crook means ill or faulty.

clue.text: Collect statement from Nick Bottom?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to gather in quantity
second meaning: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the weaver is given an ass's head, so he might confess what he now is

explanation.surface: Gathering what Shakespeare's weaver once said.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AM ASS, Bottom's confession after his transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate things in quantity.

clue.text: 100 filler note initially moved on, about to receive rating

indicators.note: moved on means shifted along, so the letter is taken out and put back further forward

parts.note: the Hungarian forint is divided into 100 fillér, so 100 fillér is one forint, I FORINT

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of note

explanation.surface: A hundred fillers move along, and someone is about to be rated.
explanation.walkthrough: Write one forint as IFORINT, then move its N forward. A rating is a telling-off, so being in for it means trouble is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in for it is to face certain punishment, here a rating, an old word for a scolding.

clue.text: Primate wee in coal scuttle

indicators.note: the small word sits in the container word

parts.note: a hod is a coal scuttle as well as a builder's carrier
Scots wee means small, as does mini

explanation.surface: A monkey, or worse, relieving itself in the coal scuttle.
explanation.walkthrough: "Wee" looks like urine but is the Scottish word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Hominids are the great-ape family, primates that include humans and their fossil relatives.

clue.text: Hired feathers on chick disappoint

parts.note: a let property is one hired out
down is the soft first plumage of a young bird

explanation.surface: A rented chick in fluffy feathers fails to live up to expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone down is to fail them, leaving them disappointed.

clue.text: Bird soon caged by people working together

indicators.note: the word for soon is enclosed by the union letters

parts.note: a trade union is workers acting together
in a mo, short for in a moment

explanation.surface: A bird about to be caged by a team of workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The tinamou is a ground-dwelling South American bird resembling a partridge.

clue.text: TMO's ruling nut has punched and passage denied

indicators.note: the nut punches a way into the ruling, sitting inside it

parts.note: in rugby the Television Match Official may rule no try
an en is a printing measure, also called a nut

explanation.surface: A rugby video referee's decision, with someone throwing punches as entry is refused.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing an en is called a nut, to tell it apart from the em (mutton).
explanation.definitionFit: No entry is the sign that forbids passage into a road or area.

clue.text: That's right — no lemon, thanks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what is right and fair
second meaning: the drinker's reply when a barman offers ice and lemon

explanation.surface: A bar exchange: asked about ice and lemon, you confirm you want only the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as JUST ICE to hear the drinker's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice is fairness, the principle that each receives what is morally due.

clue.text: Very much like the spin one gets from hot motor

definitions.meaning: first sense: a spin so enjoyable it is full of delight, read word by word
second sense: the drive taken in a stolen car, hot being slang for stolen

explanation.walkthrough: A spin is a drive; the first half reads the answer literally as a delightful ride, the second as the criminal kind in a hot, i.e. stolen, car.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyride is a reckless drive for fun, especially in a stolen vehicle.

clue.text: Suitably modulated charge sheet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a singer whose voice is well controlled is said to be in good voice
second meaning: a bill listing what is owed

explanation.surface: A charge sheet adjusted to suit, like a bill revised to the right tone.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN VOICE, a singer in good form.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill listing the charges for goods or services supplied.

clue.text: Ode composed about the closure of Man U?

definitions.note: U means socially acceptable, upper-class usage

indicators.note: the reordered poem wraps round the extra letter
a poem being composed has its words arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its last letter

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A poem written about the fall of Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: "Man U" looks like the football club; U is the upper-class label for acceptable behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: "The done thing" is correct social form, which is exactly what the U label marks as proper.

clue.text: Gem robbery liquidates stocks!

indicators.note: the words stock the answer, holding it inside them

parts.note: the gem's letters run across the end of robbery and the start of liquidates

explanation.surface: A jewel robbery wipes out the shop's stock, an exclamatory crime headline.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a mineral whose gem varieties include emerald and aquamarine.

clue.text: The birds and the bees leaving babes five slices

indicators.note: slices means cuts into, so this letter goes inside the rest
leaving means going away from, so these letters come out of babes

parts.note: the bees are the letter B written twice
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Talk of the birds and the bees leaves the babies with five slices.
explanation.walkthrough: BABES without its two Bs is AES; V cuts into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aves is the zoological class of birds, the scientific name for all birds.

clue.text: Old conflict affected supporter's group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obsolete word for battle or contest
third meaning: a faction backing someone

explanation.walkthrough: The word once meant combat, from Old English; today it means exaggeratedly mannered, or a side in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a faction of backers, a theatrical exaggerated style, and an archaic sense of battle.

clue.text: Fill up Pierre's brandy

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to cram is to fill tightly

explanation.surface: Topping up a Frenchman's brandy glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre stands for any Frenchman, marking the brandy as French.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a French spirit distilled from grape pressings left after winemaking.

clue.text: Nasty splinter from cracked instrument panel not planned

indicators.note: the splinter is taken away from the panel

parts.note: cracked tells you to break up the letters of instrument panel and reassemble them, here as the splinter's letters followed by the rest
nasty marks the word splinter as jumbled, so its letters come out of the panel in whatever order they sit

explanation.surface: A sharp sliver of plastic flies from a cracked dashboard, an accident nobody intended.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of splinter, in any order, from instrument panel and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmeant was not intended or deliberate, the same idea as unplanned.

clue.text: Counter secure at opening of Indian restaurant

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to nail is to fasten securely
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Securing a counter table at the opening night of a new Indian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: "Indian restaurant" looks like a unit, but Indian gives only its initial and the cuisine is a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian is everyday shorthand for a restaurant serving food from Italy.

clue.text: The care one's needed to fill gaps in one's education

definitions.meaning: first sense, a reverse anagram: read the answer as an instruction, TEACHER handled supply (supplely) rearranges into these two words

definitions.text: one's needed to fill gaps in one's education
definitions.meaning: second sense: a stand-in who covers lessons when the regular staff are away

explanation.surface: The attention a person needs to make up for shortfalls in their schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a reverse anagram: the answer, read as "teacher, supply", tells you to bend TEACHER into THE CARE. The rest describes a cover teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply teacher covers classes when the regular teacher is away, plugging holes in pupils' schooling.
